note: Adapted from Maiti & Chakraborty's (1994) original description (in English), the species being new in that paper; the alate (dealate specimens only), the soldier and the pseudoworker all have prose descriptions and measurements. The alate antennae are broken in the specimens, so the original does not give their segment count.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule red-brown to dark brown; antennae and labrum yellowish brown; pronotum yellowish brown to dark brown; legs golden yellow to yellowish brown; abdominal tergites pale brown, sternites pale yellow. Head hairs rather dense, those of the pronotum medium, those of the nota sparse, all long bristles. Head capsule almost circular, the width including the compound eyes far greater than the length to the base of the mandibles; Y suture visible in less strongly sclerotized specimens; frons slightly sloping in front. Compound eyes medium-sized and nearly circular, close against the base of the antennae and farther from the lower margin. Ocelli oval and translucent, touching the compound eyes and about their greatest diameter from the antennae. Postclypeus flat and narrow, almost undivided from the frons and as dark as the head capsule, with a few bristles. Anteclypeus almost trapezoidal, white and hairless. Antennae (broken in the specimens): segment 2 about half of segment 1, segment 3 slightly shorter than segment 2 and more strongly sclerotized, segment 4 the shortest, from segment 5 onwards gradually longer. Labrum broadly dome-shaped, wider than long, the distal margin nearly straight, with a few hairs on the margin and surface. Mandibles of the typical Neotermes type: left mandible with a rather long apical tooth and 2 marginal teeth, the posterior margin of the first marginal tooth equal in length to the anterior margin of the second; right mandible also with one apical tooth and 2 marginal teeth, the apical tooth finger-like, the first marginal tooth triangular, the second short with its posterior margin longer than the molar plate. Pronotum flat and slightly wider than the head capsule including the compound eyes; anterior margin rather incurved; posterior margin very weakly incurved; anterolateral angles narrowly rounded, posterolateral angles broadly rounded. Wing scales dark brown, the fore wing scale not covering the hind wing scale. At the fore wing scale the costa, subcosta, media and cubitus arise independently; the radius and radius sector arise from a common stalk and separate near the wing suture. Legs short and stout, apical tibial spur formula 3:3:3; tarsi 4-segmented; arolia present.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule pale yellow to yellowish brown, slightly darker in front; tip of the mandibles pitch-black, base yellowish brown; antennae pale brown; labrum, pronotum, legs and abdomen yellow-white. Head and thorax sparsely hairy, the abdomen more densely so. Body length (including the mandibles, excluding the antennae) 6.00—8.20 mm. Head capsule almost rectangular, far longer than wide; sides weakly convex and slightly converging in front; in lateral view the dorsal margin weakly convex, the frons gradually sloping forwards with a shallow median depression; anterolateral angles slightly projecting, posterolateral angles broadly rounded. Y suture indistinct. Eye spot whitish and indistinct. Ocelli absent. Antennae 12-segmented, segment 2 slightly shorter than segment 3, segment 3 more strongly sclerotized and conical, about one and a half times as long as segment 2; the other segments gradually longer. Left mandible with 5 marginal teeth, widely spaced with angular notches between them; posterior margin of the second marginal tooth long and nearly straight. Right mandible with 2 marginal teeth. Postmentum long and clavate, the anterior third distinctly broadened without a lateral notch; least width about one third of the greatest width; anterior margin nearly straight, posterior margin weakly concave; the anterior third with a few hairs. Pronotum narrower than the head width, sometimes about twice as long as wide, in some specimens shorter; anterior margin minutely hairy, shallowly to deeply concave but without a distinct median notch; posterior margin weakly incurved; sides convex and narrowing backwards; anterolateral angles narrowly rounded, posterolateral angles broadly rounded; surface with scattered hairs. Legs short and stout; apical tibial spur formula 3:3:3. Abdomen long; tergites and sternites rather densely hairy.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Pseudoworker: head capsule, antennae and labrum pale yellow; thorax, legs and abdomen creamy white. Head and body hairs medium. Body length (excluding the antennae) 6.53—7.48 mm. Head nearly circular, wider than long; eye spot oval, unpigmented, near the base of the antennae. Antennae 12-segmented, segment 3 incompletely divided, segment 2 about equal to segment 3, segment 4 the shortest, from segment 5 onwards gradually longer. Postclypeus flat, sparsely hairy and almost undivided from the frons. Anteclypeus transverse, the anterior margin weakly concave and hairless. Labrum far wider than long, the sides diverging forwards, the anterior margin nearly straight; dorsum rather convex, with a few short erect hairs on the surface and anterior margin. Mandibles of the typical Neotermes type. Pronotum flat, about half as long as wide; anterior margin broadly concave without a median notch; anterolateral angles broadly rounded; posterior margin nearly straight; surface with scattered long hairs, the whole margin with short hairs. Abdomen long and hairy.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Type material: soldier holotype (ZSI registration number 3165/H11), plus paratype soldiers and paratype specimens of other forms (2 dealate alates, 5 pseudoworkers, ZSI registration number 3167/H11), and paratypes at F.R.I. Dehra Dun. Type locality Haddo (Port Blair) and Chidyatapu, South Andaman, India, known only from there. Specimens collected from jamun wood and from wounds in standing trees.
